newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India sells Dec naphtha to Hanwha at minus $14.87.
newsitem.headline: India sells Dec naphtha to Hanwha at minus $14.87.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has sold by tender 25,000 tonnes of low aromatic naphtha to South Korea's Hanwha Chemical Corp at $14.87 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, on a free-on-board (fob) basis from Vizag on the east coast, industry sources said.
Traders said the award was high reflecting the good demand from North Asia.

"It is really high for Indian quality naphtha," said one trader. "Usually, this quality will be at a discount of $5 (per tonne) to c-and-f (cost-and-freight or delivered basis) to Japan (spot quotes)."
He said with freight from the Indian east coast to South Korea just below $20.00 per tonne, the award equates to a $5 premium to Japanese spot quotes.
The tender for the cargo lifting December 15-17, closed December 5 and was valid until December 6.
IOC sold its last low aromatic naphtha cargo, lifting from Bombay December 10-12 at a discount to Japanese spot quotes of around $17.33 a tonne fob Bombay on the west coast, to Dutch trader Vitol.
